text: erplots provides fluent mini-language building exposure-response plots: model curves/ribbons, summary annotation, quantile-binned response-rate/mean summaries, raw-data layer, grouped distribution panels. model-agnostic: erplots never fits model . model implementing er_predict() can visualised; implementing er_simulate() er_summary() additionally enables uncertainty spaghetti plots/VPCs model-derived summary annotations (e.g. p-values, via er_plot_add_summary() – see “summary layer independent model layer” ). See ?er_model_interface. er_plot() takes response_type = c("auto", "binary", "continuous", "count") argument (auto-detected response column given: logical values entirely {0, 1} → "binary", else "continuous"; "auto" never resolves "count" – must declared explicitly), stored object$response$type/ object$response$limits. model curve/ribbon (er_plot_add_model()) group panel (er_plot_add_groups()) layers work response type dispatch needed. quantile summary layer (er_plot_add_quantiles()) er_vpc_plot() now fully generalised across three response types (rate + Clopper-Pearson "binary"; mean + t-interval "continuous"; mean + exact Poisson interval "count"). data layer (er_plot_add_data(), renamed er_plot_show_datastrip()) also works response type, "continuous"/"count" error path left – see “Planned work” . (er_plot_add_data() went two renames: er_plot_show_datastrip() -> er_plot_show_data() -> current name, latter part naming-scheme review described “Extensibility” .) er_plot_add_data() offers two mutually exclusive structural families, selected style function passed (separate layout argument – see “Extensibility” ): default, er_style_data_overlay(), plots raw observations true (exposure, response) coordinates directly model panel – single, response-type-agnostic builder small vertical jitter applied binary responses, color aesthetic ’s always strata (sharing base plot’s legend) rather response value. er_style_data_boxjitter() (binary-response ) older panel-based design (object$part$data) – boxplot exposure values jittered points layered top, upper (responders)/lower (non-responders) panels, showing exposure distribution conditional response rather just raw points; fill means strata box color means strata points, mirroring model layer’s ribbon/line split. two structural families live separate object$part slots (overlay vs. data); passing builder one family clears slot. built-"panel"-layout builder continuous/count response – older build_data_jitter() (binary) build_data_color() (continuous/count) removed review found neither earned keep alongside er_style_data_overlay()/er_style_data_boxjitter() (see PLAN.md); custom "panel"-layout builder continuous/count remains possible via er_style_tag(), since .layer_data()’s response-type dispatch left place. er_style_data_hex() second "overlay"-layout data builder alongside er_style_data_overlay(): geom_hex()-based 2D density, N large enough raw points overplot unreadable smear (useful continuous/count responses, whose y-values spread rather piled 0/1). requires hexbin package (Suggests, guarded rlang::check_installed()). geom_hex()’s fill aesthetic already encodes bin density, ’s channel left color = strata; Tag class first, dispatch something catch: Prepending "toy_model" (rather replacing class vector) keeps every existing glm/lm method – predict(), summary(), coef(), vcov() – working via ordinary S3 inheritance; er_predict.toy_model() needs add three columns erplots wants, using stats::predict.glm() actual work: ’s whole method. ’s already enough plug mini language:  every model predict() method computes standard errors , though. nls fit doesn’t – predict.nls() silently ignores se.fit. ’s ready-made standard error, delta method (numerical gradient fitted-value function respect parameters, combined parameter covariance matrix) general-purpose fallback works differentiable mean function:  emax_fun()/finite-difference pairing deliberately hand-rolled, keep article dependency-free; real implementation likely reach numDeriv::jacobian(), – fitting function already analytic gradient available (nls() , internally) – use instead finite differences.
code: fit_toy_model <- function(formula, data, family = gaussian()) {   fit <- glm(formula, data = data, family = family)   class(fit) <- c("toy_model", class(fit))   fit }  mod <- fit_toy_model(ae1 ~ aucss, erglm_data, family = binomial()) class(mod) #> [1] "toy_model" "glm"       "lm" er_predict.toy_model <- function(model, newdata, conf_level = 0.95, ...) {   z <- -qnorm((1 - conf_level) / 2)   link <- predict(model, newdata = newdata, se.fit = TRUE, type = "link")   linkinv <- family(model)$linkinv    newdata$fit_resp <- linkinv(link$fit)   newdata$ci_lower <- linkinv(link$fit - z * link$se.fit)   newdata$ci_upper <- linkinv(link$fit + z * link$se.fit)   newdata } erglm_data |>   er_plot(aucss, ae1) |>   er_plot_add_model(mod) |>   plot() emax_fun <- function(par, aucss) {   par[["e0"]] + par[["emax"]] * aucss / (par[["ec50"]] + aucss) }  er_predict.toy_emax <- function(model, newdata, conf_level = 0.95, ...) {   z <- -qnorm((1 - conf_level) / 2)   par <- coef(model)   fit <- emax_fun(par, newdata$aucss)    eps <- 1e-6   grad <- vapply(names(par), function(nm) {     par_up <- par; par_up[nm] <- par_up[nm] + eps     par_dn <- par; par_dn[nm] <- par_dn[nm] - eps     (emax_fun(par_up, newdata$aucss) - emax_fun(par_dn, newdata$aucss)) / (2 * eps)   }, FUN.VALUE = numeric(nrow(newdata)))   se <- sqrt(rowSums((grad %*% vcov(model)) * grad))    newdata$fit_resp <- fit   newdata$ci_lower <- fit - z * se   newdata$ci_upper <- fit + z * se   newdata }  emax_mod <- nls(   biomarker_change ~ e0 + emax * aucss / (ec50 + aucss),   data = erglm_data,   start = list(e0 = -2, emax = 5, ec50 = 1000) ) class(emax_mod) <- c("toy_emax", class(emax_mod))  erglm_data |>   er_plot(aucss, biomarker_change) |>   er_plot_add_model(emax_mod) |>   plot()

code: er_simulate.toy_model <- function(model, newdata, nsim = 100, seed = NULL, ...) {   if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)    beta_hat <- coef(model)   beta_draws <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(nsim, mean = beta_hat, sigma = vcov(model))   linkinv <- family(model)$linkinv   X <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(model)), data = newdata)    reps <- vector("list", nsim)   for (i in seq_len(nsim)) {     eta <- as.vector(X %*% beta_draws[i, ])     fit_resp <- linkinv(eta)     reps[[i]] <- newdata |>       dplyr::mutate(         sim_id = i,         fit_resp = fit_resp,         # the extra ingredient `sim_resp` needs beyond `fit_resp`:         # observation-level sampling noise, appropriate to the response         # type (here, a binary draw at the simulated probability)         sim_resp = rbinom(length(fit_resp), size = 1, prob = fit_resp)       )   }   dplyr::bind_rows(reps) } erglm_data |>   er_plot(aucss, ae1) |>   er_plot_add_model(mod, style = er_style_model_spaghetti, seed = 8213) |>   plot() er_vpc_plot(   erglm_data, exposure = aucss, response = ae1, group_by = aucss,   model = mod, nsim = 50, seed = 4471 )
